content:
Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin and others attended the conference

The grand meeting commemorating the 100th birthday of Jiang Zemin was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday (17th) morning. Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the State, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, along with all current Politburo Standing Committee members, were present. Retired leaders including Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin, Zhang Dejiang, Yu Zhengsheng, Li Zhanshu, Wang Yang, Li Lanqing, Zeng Qinghong, Li Changchun, He Guoqiang, Liu Yunshan, Wang Qishan, and Zhang Gaoli also attended the meeting.

Hu Jintao not seen; Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan absent

However, Hu Jintao, who succeeded Jiang Zemin as General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, was not seen in the CCTV live broadcast. In addition, Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng, and Luo Gan, who served as Politburo Standing Committee members during the Jiang Zemin era, were also absent from this meeting.

'1989 serious political turmoil: Jiang resolutely executed the Party Central Committee's decisions'

Xi Jinping delivered an important speech at the meeting, reviewing the process of how Jiang Zemin went from Shanghai Party Secretary to becoming the core of the third-generation central collective leadership of the CPC. He specifically mentioned: 'In the spring and summer of 1989, a serious political turmoil occurred in our country. Comrade Jiang Zemin resolutely upheld and executed the correct decisions of the Party Central Committee, effectively maintaining stability in Shanghai.'

Xi Jinping also mentioned the need to learn from Jiang Zemin's 'unwavering political faith,' describing how he remained unshaken in his commitment to economic construction when confronted with major tests, including the turbulent international landscape of the late 1980s and early 1990s and the serious domestic political turmoil. He also emphasized approaches such as the principle that governing the country must begin with governing the Party, and that governing the Party must be strict.

Xi Jinping also stated that there is a need to learn from Jiang Zemin's 'forward-looking strategic thinking,' mentioning that Jiang Zemin led the successful return of Hong Kong and Macau during his tenure, as well as promoting the reaching of the '1992 Consensus' between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, which embodies the one-China principle.

Outside observers are paying attention to Beijing's holding of a grand commemoration of Jiang Zemin's 100th birthday at this time, as well as the political signals conveyed by Xi Jinping's speech.

Independent political scholar Chen Daoyin stated that holding grand commemoration activities on the 100th birthday of a late leader is a institutional convention. Many important leaders in the past, such as Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, have had grand 100th birthday commemoration events held for them. As the core of the CPC's third-generation collective leadership, it is consistent with convention and standard for Jiang Zemin to have a grand commemoration held for his 100th birthday.

Scholar: The 1989 remarks contain no new formulations

Regarding Xi Jinping taking the initiative to mention Jiang Zemin's political stance in 1989 during the commemoration, Chen Daoyin believes that 1989 was an important turning point for Chinese politics and Jiang Zemin's political career. Because Jiang Zemin 'chose the right side' that year, he was elevated from a local leader on the verge of retirement to being urgently appointed to Beijing to replace Zhao Ziyang, becoming the core of the CPC's third-generation central collective leadership. Therefore, when reviewing his life, the events of 1989 must be mentioned.

Chen Daoyin said that Jiang Zemin's resolute upholding of the Party Central Committee's decisions at that time echoes the political requirement of 'two upholds' currently emphasized by Xi Jinping, hence the need to reiterate it. He also believes that Xi Jinping's remarks regarding 1989 are all 'definitive verdicts' and do not offer any new formulations; there is no need for outside observers to over-interpret Xi Jinping's revisiting of 1989.

As for the grand commemoration of Jiang Zemin's 100th birthday, Hu Jintao, as the core of the CPC's fourth-generation collective leadership, was absent. Chen Daoyin said that although retired leaders are not necessarily required to attend such events, logically, Hu Jintao, as Jiang Zemin's successor, should have attended a grand event commemorating Jiang Zemin. His absence may be due to reasons such as not being in Beijing or being unwell. He pointed out that attention can be paid on Tuesday (18th) at Zhu Rongji's farewell ceremony to see whether Hu Jintao sends a wreath.

Zhao Jianmin, former dean of the College of Social Sciences at Chinese Culture University in Taiwan, who specializes in the study of China's political development and cross-strait relations, believes that Xi Jinping's speech today is a comprehensive review of Jiang Zemin's life. Several important key points of Jiang Zemin's political career—including proposing the important thought of the 'Three Represents,' the reaching of the '1992 Consensus' across the strait, and his resolute support for the Party Central Committee's decisions in 1989—are all unavoidable content when reviewing Jiang Zemin.

Zhao Jianmin said that Xi Jinping only mentioned Jiang Zemin's resolute stand with the Party Central Committee in 1989, and did not make further remarks on the June 4th incident, which is a normal handling.

Zhao Jianmin also pointed out that Xi Jinping's emphasis on Jiang Zemin's 100th birthday also has personal factors. He believes that Xi Jinping's later promotion, from a leader in Fujian to successively taking charge as the 'top leader' of major economic provinces Zhejiang and Shanghai, laid the foundation for his rise to the highest leadership level. Jiang Zemin played an important and crucial role in this process.

He believes that Xi Jinping's emphasis on commemorating Jiang Zemin demonstrates, on one hand, Xi Jinping's sentimentality and gratitude. On the other hand, by evaluating Jiang Zemin, Xi Jinping emphasizes his promotion of strict Party governance and anti-corruption work, which can also show that these policies are an inheritance and continuation of the work direction from the Jiang Zemin era. This represents the implementation of approaches that already have consensus within the Party, and serves to clarify rumors circulating among the public.

To highlight the importance of obeying the Party Central Committee at critical moments of right and wrong

However, veteran Chinese political commentator Cai Shenkun holds a different view. He described Xi Jinping's public mention of Jiang Zemin's stance during the 1989 'political turmoil' as rare, and pointed out that during Jiang Zemin's lifetime, as well as after his death by his family, there was a desire to downplay rather than emphasize how Jiang Zemin rose to the center of supreme power because of the June 4th incident.

Cai Shenkun believes that Xi Jinping's special emphasis on this point this time is intended to highlight the importance of obeying the Party Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty at critical moments of right and wrong.

In addition, Cai Shenkun pointed out that the 21st National Congress of the Communist Party of China (abbreviated as the 'CPC 21st National Congress') is expected to be convened next autumn. He believes that Xi Jinping's emphasis on Jiang Zemin's 100th birthday, as well as his commendation of Jiang Zemin's resolute choice to support the Party Central Committee, can, on one hand, emphasize the political lineage between himself and Jiang Zemin, strengthening the legitimacy of his political continuity. On the other hand, by commemorating Jiang Zemin, he can also reiterate to Party members the importance of obeying the Central Committee and political loyalty.
